text.what: Putting bunches into the fermenter with their stems still attached, instead of pulling the berries off first. Stems bring water, potassium, tannin and a green-stalk smell that turns spicy when it works and stalky when it doesn't.
text.how: Stems raise pH by absorbing acid, cool the ferment by taking up heat, and build a lattice that lets a cap breathe. Growers pick a percentage — 30%, 50%, all of it — and argue about it forever. Ripe lignified stems help; green ones taste like the pruning pile.

kin.as: The French word, and its root.
The other half of the same fermentation decision.
A variety thin enough in tannin to notice what the stems add.
